text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed the OpenAPI examples for POST /v1/generate use "input" while the SDK snippets (python/js) use "prompt". That will confuse customers when they copy/paste. Also the Python example is missing max_new_tokens and the curl example shows an array for the response but the schema is an object.

nick: Ah good catch. Is this the PR at https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/312 ? I skimmed but missed the examples.

maya: Yes that one. I left inline comments but wanted to coordinate before pushing changes.

sam: Quick note on the response shape — the OpenAPI currently defines:
text_2:
```json
  responses:
    200:
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            type: array
            items:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/GenerateResponse'
```
text_3:
But our runtime returns an object with `id`, `choices` (array), `meta`. So the schema should be `type: object` with `properties.choices` as array. I can send a patch for components/schemas/GenerateResponse to match.

jordan: Also the streaming example in the API ref shows SSE events like `event: token` which we don't emit — we use bare data frames and `event: done` only for explicit end. That mismatch will break SSE clients.

maya: Great catches. Proposed plan: (1) standardize request param name to `prompt` everywhere and add a short migration note in the changelog; (2) change response schema to object + update examples; (3) fix streaming example to show correct SSE payloads and add a short note for SDK users about how streaming maps to SDK callbacks.

nick: I can own (1) and the migration blurb. I'll open a tiny PR that updates the OpenAPI examples + the Python and JS snippets in the same commit so copies match. PR link will be posted here.

sam: I'll take (2) — update components/schemas/GenerateResponse and adjust the example outputs (curl/python examples). I'll also add a quick unit test that validates example JSON against the schema so this doesn't regress.

jordan: I'll handle (3) — I'll add a short snippet showing how to parse the raw SSE stream in Node and mention that some client libs will abstract that away. Example:
text_5:
maya: docs-bot flagged the PR in CI — failing check is `openapi-lint/examples` (missing required `max_new_tokens` example value). I can add that to your PR, @nick, unless you prefer to include it.

docs-bot: CI | openapi-lint/examples failed — example request bodies must include required numeric fields. See https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/ci/12345 for logs.

nick: I'll add max_new_tokens=64 to the examples and push. Planning to bundle changes tonight.

sam: One more small question — in the Python SDK snippet we currently do `client.generate(input="...")`. I'll change it to `client.generate(prompt="...")` but should we keep a compatibility note about accepting `input` as an alias? Backend accepts both via schema coercion.

maya: Let's add a one-line note: "Deprecated alias: `input` — will be removed in next major. Use `prompt` moving forward." Saves users time and is honest.

jordan: After patches land, can we run a quick smoke on internal examples site? I'll run through the SSE demo and the curl examples. Ping me when PRs merged.

nick: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/319 — includes example sync+stream updates, migration note, and max_new_tokens fix.

sam: Merged my schema patch into that PR. Also added the schema validation test under tests/examples_test.py.

maya: Thanks all. After merge, I'll update the docs changelog and add a small note in the SDK migration guide.

jordan: Verified SSE example locally — looks good. :thumbsup:

maya: Closing loop: once PR merged, I'll deploy the docs preview and leave a comment here with the preview URL. Thanks!
